scope: Approval policy: who may retire or supersede a requirement (the CODEOWNERS policy). Belongs here: the CODEOWNERS approval policy only. Does not belong here: the loss-detection mechanism itself (→ GUARD). Boundary case: OWNER keeps only the CODEOWNERS approval policy while GOV-01's disappearance-detection concept lives in GUARD.

requirements.statement: A status flip to `superseded`/`retired` requires the domain owner's approval (CODEOWNERS on the spec path); otherwise gate red.
requirements.why: Retiring or superseding a requirement is a governance act — it needs the owner's approval, enforced via CODEOWNERS.

requirements.statement: When a change flips a requirement's status into superseded or deprecated on a spec path with CODEOWNERS domain owners and no domain owner is in the approver set, spec check shall report UNAPPROVED_STATUS_FLIP — warning severity by default, error severity under --require-owner-approval.
requirements.why: Ending a requirement's life is a governance act; without the owner check, anyone who can edit the spec file can end a requirement and the CODEOWNERS policy is decorative.
